To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
redox-insensitive POU domain of human Oct1 transcription factors was crystallized in complex with different POU dimer binding DNA elements.
the redox-insensitive POU domain of Oct1 was crystallized with two POU dimer binding elements.
the POU domain can form crystals in complex with two different DNA-response elements and that the redox sensitivity of the POU-domain cysteine is a critical factor for crystallization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the crystallization of protein-DNA cocrystallization and with the characterization of the DNA-binding specificity of the human Oct-1 transcription factor.
the development of a general approach to crystallizing proteins that bind to DNA.
the structural basis of transcription factor binding to DNA and with the regulation of the transcription factor activity by redox-sensitive cysteine residues in the POU domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the redox-insensitive mutant of the human Oct-1 POU-domain was crystallized with two POU-dimer binding DNA elements.
the POU domain of Oct1 can be crystallized with different POU dimer-binding DNA elements, provided that the redox state of the protein is controlled.
the crystallization of protein-DNA cocrystallization is not an easy task, and that a lot of time and patience is required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a redox-insensitivity of the protein-DNA interaction is required for crystallization of protein-DNA cocrystal complexes.
the POU domain can be crystallized in complex with DNA.
a protein-DNA complex can be obtained for crystallization only if both components are stable under the crystallization conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the redox sensitivity of the protein-DNA interaction has to be considered when crystallizing transcription factors.
redox-insensitive versions of POU domains are required for successful crystallization.
redox-sensitive cysteines can prevent crystallization of a protein-DNA complex.
